Weapons manufacturers and military delegations from around the world are in Qatar for one of the Middle East’s largest defence gatherings, the Doha International Maritime Defence Exhibition (DIMDEX).
This year’s event stands out not only for the scale of military hardware on display, but also for its timing amid heightened geopolitical tensions from the Gulf to the Red Sea.
DIMDEX focuses on next-generation naval technologies, integrated defence systems and the need for fast, data-driven responses on the battlefield.
Recent regional incidents, including missile activity linked to tensions with Iran, underline the growing importance of maritime security.
But the exhibition is more than a showcase of equipment; it reinforces Qatar’s role as a global diplomatic convener and deal-making hub for defence leaders.
The gathering provides a snapshot of shifting alliances, military modernisation and how power is being projected along critical sea routes.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Al Jazeera was taken inside a vast tunnel network in the Raqqa countryside, built by the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF). Syrian government forces have been searching the underground passages since the SDF withdrew, with the tunnels reportedly used for weapons storage. The tunnel visited was large enough for trucks or buses and was still under construction, with debris suggesting work had recently been ongoing. Local residents said the SDF restricted access to the area and that the region is full of tunnels, though no one knows their exact purpose. The report highlights how the SDF relied heavily on underground routes beneath towns and villages. The Syrian army accompanied the journalists during the visit, emphasising the government’s control over the area after the SDF pullback. The discovery raises questions about the extent of the SDF’s underground infrastructure and its role in the conflict.

description:
The death toll from a fire at a shopping mall in Karachi over the weekend has risen to at least 26, according to Pakistani authorities, as the search for more than 50 missing people continues.
South deputy inspector general of police, Syed Asad Raza, told the Dawn newspaper on Monday that eight more bodies had been recovered since Sunday evening by rescue personnel, taking the death toll from six to 14.
Karachi is Pakistan’s largest city and the capital of the southern Sindh province.
The fire broke out late on Saturday at the Gul Plaza shopping mall, a densely packed commercial complex. Firefighters managed to bring the massive blaze under control after about 36 hours, allowing rescue teams to enter the building to rescue those trapped inside.

Al Jazeera’s Kamal Hyder reports from the mall in Karachi.
